rows.behavior: Each specialist group can send its small, true, local concern through its own channel to a different partnership member.
Members can meet on the recurring weekly schedule to review concerns and work toward an activation decision.
Consideration of the local concerns can consume meeting time and slow progress toward the decision.
A relevant concern can cause members to reopen an issue that had previously been treated as settled.
A member can change from undecided or supportive to conditionally supportive until a relevant concern is addressed.
If deliberations, readiness, or support remain insufficient, the partnership can delay activation rather than deploy immediately.
If required support or readiness is absent by the deadline, activation can be blocked.
If the partnership obtains sufficient support and readiness by the deadline, it can activate and deploy the early-warning system.

unsupported: The schema cannot encode a formal voting rule, veto structure, or required number of supportive members without one being supplied.
The schema cannot directly enforce that a concern affects only its local scope; that constraint is represented descriptively and in provenance.
The schema cannot model the technical operation or epidemiological performance of the bio-surveillance system in detail.
